title: feat: Add dissection support for SSH protocol extensions (RFC8308)
description:
This PR adds SSH dissection support for the SSH_MSG_EXT_INFO message from RFC 8308 as well as commonly used extensions and their protocol messages (if any).

Added dissection support for the following SSH protocol messages:

- `SSH_MSG_EXT_INFO`
- `SSH_MSG_NEWCOMPRESS`
- `SSH_MSG_PING`
- `SSH_MSG_PONG`

`SSH_MSG_PING` and `SSH_MSG_PONG` were introduced in OpenSSH 9.5 as part of their keystroke timing attack countermeasure and uses the message code range for local extensions (>= 192). A client may send `SSH_MSG_PING` if the server included the `ping@openssh.com` extension in their `SSH_MSG_EXT_INFO`. As the message code range for local extensions may be used for other purposes, this PR restricts dissection of SSH_MSG_PING and `SSH_MSG_PONG` to those connections where `ping@openssh.com` is present.

Added dissection support for the following SSH extensions:

- `server-sig-algs`
- `delay-compression`
- `no-flow-control`
- `elevation`
- `publickey-algorithms@roumenpetrov.info`

There are other commonly used extensions (for example, `ping@openssh.com`). Those extensions do not contain structured extension values that require advanced dissection, but rather empty extension values or a single byte indicating the extension's version.

Hi Fabian, look good, do you have some pcap ?

Yes, sure. Find attached a sample SSH capture between an OpenSSH 9.6p1 client and an OpenSSH 9.5p1 server. As the SSH_MSG_EXT_INFO is sent encrypted, I have also attached the keylog file for the captured connection (note: you may have to restart wireshark when changing the keylog for it to take effect). The capture file contains the following messages and extensions:

- `SSH_MSG_EXT_INFO`
- `SSH_MSG_PING`
- `SSH_MSG_PONG`
- `server-sig-algs`
- `publickey-hostbound@openssh.com`
- `ping@openssh.com`
